concept-intro.rationale: Prose introducing the 'less is more' principle: visual aids support rather than replace the spoken content. When they become the focus, effectiveness dwindles.

coupling.note: Uncoupled — the weak/strong slide distinction is universal, not discipline-specific. An overloaded slide is overloaded regardless of subject. No pack variation needed; same images serve all contexts. FCI-1 satisfied trivially.

interior.rationale: The outcomes ask learners to distinguish visual aids that carry a point from those that carry a script, and to recognise supporting features. A weak/strong slide comparison — overloaded vs clean — makes the principle concrete. Narrative's forced sequential progression presents the weaker version first, matching evaluate-versions pedagogy. FIRST USE of narrative for evaluate-versions; pattern amended at R53 to admit it for visual artefact comparison.

practical-guidance.rationale: The book's recommendations distilled: less is more, bold sparingly, avoid small fonts, complementary fonts, accessible colours, keywords not sentences, graphics over text, check resolution. Prose checklist rather than interactive checklist because this is guidance to internalise, not a reusable working tool.

decidedValue.note: Interior uses the newly-amended activity-patterns/evaluate-versions (R53 amendment: narrative added for visual artefact comparison). This is the first lesson in the programme where the weak/strong pair is visual rather than prose.

workedExampleDesign.format: weak/strong visual comparison via narrative slideshow

itemStructure.label: Weak slide
itemStructure.description: Cluttered, text-heavy slide that functions as a script. Full sentences, small font, no white space, no focal point. The speaker would read from this rather than speak to it.

itemStructure.label: Strong slide
itemStructure.description: Clean slide with a header, 3-4 keywords as triggers, one high-impact image. White space, large readable font, clear focal point. The speaker speaks to it; the slide supports, not replaces.

workedExampleDesign.teachingPoint: The weak slide carries a script; the strong slide carries a point. The learner sees the contrast and recognises what makes visual aids effective: simplicity, supporting role, speaker-centred design.
workedExampleDesign.note: Narrative presents weak first, strong second — forced sequential order matches the evaluate-versions pedagogy of showing what doesn't work before showing what does.

grounding.ref: p.209 'less is more' and design recommendations
